OpenAIQRH, original PDF p.4 Theorem 1.1, with its proof concluded on p.197, gives $\Re \rho\le 7/8$ for all nontrivial zeros of $\zeta $; it does not exclude equality. Under B1 we have instead $\Re \rho\le 27/32$. In fact for $\Re  s>1$, Euler product and integration by parts give
$$
-\frac {\zeta '(s)}{\zeta (s)}=\frac {s}{s-1}+s\int _1^\infty (\psi (t)-t)t^{-s-1}\,dt.
$$
The integral on $[1,e^{200}]$ is holomorphic; on $[e^{200},\infty )$ the exact contract gives locally normally convergent integrals (even after differentiation) for $\Re  s>27/32$. A zero would give a pole of the logarithmic derivative, which the continued expression does not have there. No boundary exclusion is claimed. This proves an earlier usable consequence than the starting point of the direct majorant; it does **not** apply that direct majorant below $e^{200}$. The constant $1/64$ and threshold are used as given in this argument, but the resulting zero boundary would follow with any finite coefficient and cutoff at the same power with this logarithmic factor. The direct branch $v^2e^{-5v/32}/64$ still enters minima where legal.

Platt--Trudgian FiniteRH, original PDF p.2 Thm 1, gives RH for $|\Im \rho |\le 3000175332800$, larger than $H$. Real zeros with $0<s<1$ are absent also by the alternating series for $(1-2^{1-s})\zeta (s)$ (strictly positive by pairing terms). Consequently all zeros in the high-real-part sums below have $|\Im \rho |>H$. Conjugate zeros are counted with multiplicity. The sources are used as stated, not re-proved by this packet.

FKS PDF p.7 $2.14$, Cor.2.9, and pp.26–27 Table 8 **first block, $a_1=0.77$** give for $t\ge  H$
$$
 N(s,t)\le  c_1 t^k(\log  t)^q+c_2(\log  t)^2,\qquad 
 k=\tfrac83(1-s),\quad  q=5-2s .
$$
Use the rows in cert.py (upward padded), on their stated $s$-intervals. Only $3/4\le  s<7/8$ is needed. FKS p.4 defines $N(s,t)$ with $\Re \rho\ge s$ and $0<\Im \rho<t$. We use its bound for the subset $\Re \rho>s$, and at closed ordinate endpoints use the right limit of the continuous majorant. Equalities at internal real-part cuts are assigned to the bin on their **left**. No bound from the prospective $0.618$ block is needed. With $h=\log  H, d=1-k$, let
$$
 J(h)=\sum _{j=0}^3 \binom{3}{j}h^{-j}
 \left (\frac {j!}{d^{j+1}}+\frac {(q-3)(j+1)!}{h d^{j+2}}\right ),
\quad 
 C(s)=2\left [c_1 H^{-d}h^q J(h)+c_2H^{-1}(h^2+2h+2)\right ].
$$
This bounds $2\sum _{\beta >s,\gamma >H}1/\gamma $. Partial summation passes to infinity since $k<1$. For the integral substitute $t=H e^z$, use $(1+z/h)^{q-3}\le 1+(q-3)z/h$, and integrate the polynomial times $e^{-dz}$. This removes the log-power loss on the capped zeros. The same proof bounds the tail $\gamma >T\ge  H$ with $H,h$ replaced by $T,\log  T$: the lower boundary contribution $-N(s,T)/T$ can be discarded.

For cap $b$ take cuts $s_0=3/4<s_1<\cdots <s_m<b$, the grid of spacing $1/2000$, and set $s_{m+1}=b$. At each cut take $C_j=\min _{i\le  j}C(s_i)$, using optionally outward rational rounding before the minimum (the executable uses this option). Put $C_{m+1}=0$ and
$$
 Z_b(v)=\sum _{j=0}^m (C_j-C_{j+1})e^{-(1-s_{j+1})v}.
$$
Indeed the total weighted exponential is at most
$$
 C_0 e^{-(1-s_1)v}+\sum _{j=1}^m C_j
 (e^{-(1-s_{j+1})v}-e^{-(1-s_j)v}).
$$
This follows by charging each bin its right endpoint and using the upper bounds on cumulative masses; expanding gives the displayed nonnegative exponential mixture. Thus $Z_b$ bounds the conjugate-pair-weighted high-zero sum with denominator $\gamma $, which bounds the same sum with $|\rho |$ or $|\rho -1|$. There is no factor of two left to insert. Truncating the grid at $27/32$ instead of $7/8$ makes $Z_b(v)$ strictly smaller for $v>0$ in this construction $(C_j>0)$; weight on subsequent increments has actually been removed. A finer grid, or taking the left limit of a density row when legitimate, gives further variants by the same proof. The displayed grid is the one used for the certificates.

$$
The integral on $[1,e^{200}]$ is holomorphic; on $[e^{200},\infty )$ the exact contract gives locally normally convergent integrals (even after differentiation) for $\Re  s>27/32$. FKS PDF p.7 $2.14$, Cor.2.9, and pp.26–27 Table 8 **first block, $a_1=0.77$** give for $t\ge  H$
$$
 N(s,t)\le  c_1 t^k(\log  t)^q+c_2(\log  t)^2,\qquad 
 k=\tfrac83(1-s),\quad  q=5-2s .
$$
Use the rows in cert.py (upward padded), on their stated $s$-intervals. Only $3/4\le  s<7/8$ is needed. FKS p.4 defines $N(s,t)$ with $\Re \rho\ge s$ and $0<\Im \rho<t$. We use its bound for the subset $\Re \rho>s$, and at closed ordinate endpoints use the right limit of the continuous majorant. Equalities at internal real-part cuts are assigned to the bin on their **left**. No bound from the prospective $0.618$ block is needed. With $h=\log  H, d=1-k$, let
$$
 J(h)=\sum _{j=0}^3 \binom{3}{j}h^{-j}
 \left (\frac {j!}{d^{j+1}}+\frac {(q-3)(j+1)!}{h d^{j+2}}\right ),
\quad 
 C(s)=2\left [c_1 H^{-d}h^q J(h)+c_2H^{-1}(h^2+2h+2)\right ].
$$
This bounds $2\sum _{\beta >s,\gamma >H}1/\gamma $. Partial summation passes to infinity since $k<1$. For the integral substitute $t=H e^z$, use $(1+z/h)^{q-3}\le 1+(q-3)z/h$, and integrate the polynomial times $e^{-dz}$. This removes the log-power loss on the capped zeros. The same proof bounds the tail $\gamma >T\ge  H$ with $H,h$ replaced by $T,\log  T$: the lower boundary contribution $-N(s,T)/T$ can be discarded.

For cap $b$ take cuts $s_0=3/4<s_1<\cdots <s_m<b$, the grid of spacing $1/2000$, and set $s_{m+1}=b$. At each cut take $C_j=\min _{i\le  j}C(s_i)$, using optionally outward rational rounding before the minimum (the executable uses this option). Put $C_{m+1}=0$ and
$$
 Z_b(v)=\sum _{j=0}^m (C_j-C_{j+1})e^{-(1-s_{j+1})v}.
$$
Indeed the total weighted exponential is at most
$$
 C_0 e^{-(1-s_1)v}+\sum _{j=1}^m C_j
 (e^{-(1-s_{j+1})v}-e^{-(1-s_j)v}).
$$
This follows by charging each bin its right endpoint and using the upper bounds on cumulative masses; expanding gives the displayed nonnegative exponential mixture. Thus $Z_b$ bounds the conjugate-pair-weighted high-zero sum with denominator $\gamma $, which bounds the same sum with $|\rho |$ or $|\rho -1|$. There is no factor of two left to insert. Truncating the grid at $27/32$ instead of $7/8$ makes $Z_b(v)$ strictly smaller for $v>0$ in this construction $(C_j>0)$; weight on subsequent increments has actually been removed. A finer grid, or taking the left limit of a density row when legitimate, gives further variants by the same proof. The displayed grid is the one used for the certificates.

Let $n=38358837682$. Define $r_*$ as the unique root in $(n,n+1)$ of
$$
 \frac{et}{\log t}\cdot 632207037=1644673232^2.
$$
Then **$R(x)>0$ for every real $x>r_*$**, and $R(r_*)=0$. At integer arguments the least inclusive permanent onset is $n+1$. The root lies strictly between $n+0.217926365$ and $n+0.217926366$. In particular a sufficient inclusive real onset is $n+0.217926366$. The strict ray cannot extend left of $r_*$, and replacing that open endpoint by a closed one would be false.

Here are the proof and trust details. pcount.cpp and endpoint.py independently count
$\pi(n)=\pi(n+1)=1644673232$ and $\pi(14111427770)=632207037$. The certified interval for $x/e$ throughout $[n,n+1]$ lies strictly between 14111427770 and 14111427771, so both counts are constant there. $et/\log  t$ is strictly increasing there. The checked endpoint signs and exact root give the assertion in that unit interval, including the counterexample at $n+0.001$ by monotonicity. The literal all-real left endpoint of Platt--Trudgian PNT (arXiv:1809.03134v2), PDF p.3 Thm.2, should not be imported: it conflicts with these reproducible counts. We use the inherited integer finite computation above $n$ to $10^{11}$ (Dudek--Platt arXiv:1407.1901v1 PDF p.8, 'Computation'; not their RH-dependent infinite tail). In each $[m,m+1)$ for $m\ge n+1$, the first count $\pi(x)$ is constant and $\pi(x/e)$ is nondecreasing, so $R(x)\ge  R(m)>0$. The remaining finite segment through $1.15\cdot10^{16}$ is Dudek--Platt Lemma 3.4 (PDF p.10). That finite evidence is inherited, not a new replay of the enormous verification. The independently derived analytic tail starts already at $L=36.9$, with $e^{36.9}<1.15\cdot10^{16}$. Thus the misworded PNT Thm.2 is not needed for **any** part of our connected-domain proof. Neither the B0 nor the B1 sign theorem uses full RH. The published disjoint sign domains and the original tails at $e^{3915}$, $e^{9658}$ need not be used beyond the finite segment.

The integer counter program stores the descending distinct quotients $v=\lfloor  N/i\rfloor $, initially with count (v-1). When processing a prime $p$, the data count numbers (ge2) with no prime factor below $p$, together with the already processed primes. $p$ survives precisely when the counts at (p,p-1) differ; if $v\ge  p^2$, remove precisely the (pm) with (mge p) surviving that test, numbering $S(\lfloor  v/p\rfloor )-S(p-1)$. The child quotient occurs in the same list and is smaller, hence not yet updated on that pass. All $1\le  v\le \lfloor \sqrt  N\rfloor $ occur as a contiguous suffix; for larger $v$ the zero-based index is $\lfloor  N/v\rfloor -1$. After processing through $\lfloor \sqrt  N\rfloor $ the survivors at $N$ are exactly the primes. All integers fit in the specified machine widths. endpoint.py also checks end signs by outward decimal intervals with the proof contract in notes.md.

$$

$$
On (Lge34) we have $P_{27}(L)\le  A(L)\le  1+1/L+3/L^2=U_A(L)$, with $P_N=\sum _{j=0}^N j!L^{-j}$. Indeed $P_N'+\kappa  P_N=1-(N+1)!L^{-N-1}$, while $U_A'+\kappa  U_A=1+L^{-2}-9L^{-3}\ge 1$. $$

$$
using $z/(1-z)\le 1$ in the omitted geometric tail. It is positive. In the differential comparison, subtract $(d/dL+\kappa )\sum _{n=4}^{27}g_nz^n$ from $(1-z)D(z)^2$. def coeff(v):
    v=I(v)
    return ((v-2*(v/(pi*e)).log())**2-4)/(8*pi)

def bound(l,u): # combined normalized v^4 error on [l,u] within [34,58]
    assert l>=34 and u<=58
    v=I(l)

def los(l,u,signed):

    m=bound(l-1,u-1)*(I(l)/(l-1))**5
    return m if signed else m+2*Alim(l)*d+d*d/I(l)**4

           for j in range(max(N-3,len(target)))]
    m=D('Infinity'); at=None

def finite(l,u,N,mode,target,step=Q(1,8),start_n=0):
    # target is polynomial in 1/L, with nonnegative coefficient list
    diff=[(g(j+4) if j+4<=N else 0)-(target[j] if j<len(target) else 0)
           for j in range(max(N-3,len(target)))]
    m=D('Infinity'); at=None
    while l<u:
        r=min(u,l+step)
        low=sum(I(c)/I(r if c>=0 else l)**j for j,c in enumerate(diff))-loss(l,r,mode)
        if low.a<m:m,at=low.a,l
        l=r
    print('finite',mode,target,'slack',f'{m:.8E}','at',at)
    assert m>0
def tail(l,N,mode,target,verbose=True):
    # by L>=l, L^4 loss <= l^4 loss provided l>= threshold of each exponential term.
    # All target coefficients except radius correction are nonnegative residuals.
    j=next(j for j in range(N-3) if (g(j+4)-(target[j] if j<len(target) else 0))>0)
    sub=target+[0]*(N-3-len(target))
    assert all(g(n)-sub[n-4]>=0 for n in range(4,N+1))
    assert l-1>=Q(6+j)/Q(1,8) and l>=59
    # use just spectral branch for tail, also when CH happens to be smaller
    def one(v):
        S=S1 if mode else S0
        return sum(c*I(v)**(4+k)*(-I(a)*v).exp()*(1+1/(I(v)*(1-a-2/J))) for c,a,k in S+powers)+(2*I(v)**5/25)*(-I(v)+29).exp()
    d=one(l);m=one(l-1)*(I(l)/(l-1))**5
    assert ((m+2*Alim(l)*d+d*d/I(l)**4)*I(l)**j).b < I(g(j+4)-sub[j]).a
    if verbose: print('tail',mode,'L>=',l,'leading residual degree',j)

All variables $x$ and $L=\log  x$ are real, and the sums include $p=x$ when $x$ is prime. Use the two nested premise sets B0 and B1 from spectral.md. Define
$$
\begin{aligned}
 P&=\prod_{p\le x}(1-1/p),\qquad Q=1/P,\\
 \mathcal R&=\sum_{p\le x}1/p-(\log L+M),\\
 \mathcal G&=\sum_{p\le x}(\log p)/p-(L-B_3),\\
 M&=\gamma+\sum_p(\log(1-1/p)+1/p),\qquad
 B_3=\gamma+\sum_p\frac{\log p}{p(p-1)}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Define
$$
 U(L)=\sum _{n\le  e^L}\frac {\Lambda (n)}n-(L-\gamma ),\qquad 
 W(L)=\sum _{n\le  e^L}\frac {\Lambda (n)}{n\log  n}-\log  L-\gamma 
$$
$the (n=1) term in the \log -weighted \sum  is omitted$. Integration by parts gives
$$
 U(L)=E(L)-\int _L^\infty  E(v)\,dv,\qquad 
 W(L)=\frac {E(L)}L-\int _L^\infty  E(v)(1/v+1/v^2)\,dv
       =\frac {U(L)}L-\int _L^\infty  U(v)/v^2\,dv. \tag {M1}
$$
To see the constants if deriving these identities from scratch: the spectral bounds ensure the integrable error and hence the existence of $lim (\sum \Lambda (n)/n-L)$. Its value is the constant Laurent term $-\gamma $ of $-\zeta '/\zeta (1+h)$ by the Abelian integral with kernel $h e^{-hv}$. The Laurent term follows from $\zeta (1+h)-1/h\to\gamma $, obtained by subtracting $\int _n^{n+1}t^{-1-h}dt$ termwise from $n^{-1-h}$; the remainder is holomorphic near $h=0$. For $W$, the limit of the error is 0 by Dusart Thm.5.6 and the convergent prime-power series $\gamma -M$. Thus integration on a finite interval followed by a limit proves (M1), with correct signs.

def tails(L):
    # normalized by 1 and by 1/L (i.e. L*upper bound for log prime powers)
    v=I(L)
    c=I('1.000000147');delta=I('166.64')/v**3
    w=(2*c-1+delta)*(-v/2).exp()+I('2.67')*(-2*v/3).exp()
    t=(2*(1+1/v)*c-1+delta)*(-v/2).exp()+I('2.67')*(1+1/v)*(-2*v/3).exp()
    return w,t

def phi_tail(L,m):
    J=Q(190 if m==0 else 169)
    S=S0 if m==0 else S1
    if L>=J: return ev(S,L),im(S,L)
    j=m_tail(m)+im(CH,max(L,58),J)
    if L>=58:return ev(CH,L),j
    j+=im(B,max(L,K),58)
    if L>=K:return ev(B,L),j
    return ev(A,L), j+im(A,L,K)
def tails(L):
    # normalized by 1 and by 1/L (i.e. L*upper bound for log prime powers)
    v=I(L)
    c=I('1.000000147');delta=I('166.64')/v**3
    w=(2*c-1+delta)*(-v/2).exp()+I('2.67')*(-2*v/3).exp()
    t=(2*(1+1/v)*c-1+delta)*(-v/2).exp()+I('2.67')*(1+1/v)*(-2*v/3).exp()
    return w,t
def piecewise(l,u):
    # E on block clipped to one Phi piece, bound decreasing E, J from its left endpoint.
    v=I(l); w=I(u)
    F,J=phi_tail(l,0)
    if l<K:

    else: WV=F/v+(1/v+1/v**2)*J
    tW,tP=tails(l)
    W=WV+tP/v
    U=F+J+tW
    return ((W.exp()-1)*w**3, W*w**3,U*w**2)

def after(l,u):

def spectralparts(m):
    a=Q(1,8) if m==0 else Q(5,32)
    S=S0 if m==0 else S1
    Z=S[4:]
    D=S[:4]+[(I(12),a+Q(1,6),4),(I(15),a+Q(1,2),2)]
    return a,Z,D
def pure(L,m):
    a,Z,rem=spectralparts(m)
    v=I(L); z=ev(Z,L); d=ev(rem,L); j=im(rem,L)
    w,t=tails(L)
    # L times log error, and weighted sum error
    tlog=(1+2/(3000000000000*v))*z+d+(1+1/v)*j+t
    tw=z+d+j+w
    x=tlog/v
    # exp(x)-1 <= x/(1-x) (x>=0, x<1), without cancellation
    tprod=tlog/(1-x)
    res=I(a*L).exp()
    return tprod*res,tlog*res,tw*res

def anch(l,u):
    v,w=I(l),I(u)
    negR=(-ev(dn,l)/v-(1/L0+1/L0**2)*im(dn,L0,w)).a
    posR=(-ev(up,u)/w-(1/w+1/w**2)*(im(up,L0,v) if v.a>=L0.b else I(0))).b
    negG=(-ev(dn,l)-im(dn,L0,w)).a
    posG=(-ev(up,u)-(im(up,L0,v) if v.a>=L0.b else I(0))).b
    br=R+I(negR,posR)
    bg=G+I(negG,posG)
    be=I(max(br.b,hi(lambda:br.a.copy_negate()+D('0.00000000025'))))
    return [(be.exp()-1)*w**3,I(max(br.b,br.a.copy_negate()))*w**3,I(max(bg.b,bg.a.copy_negate()))*w**2]

def pure(L,m):
    a,Z,rem=spectralparts(m)
    v=I(L); z=ev(Z,L); d=ev(rem,L); j=im(rem,L)
    w,t=tails(L)
    # L times log error, and weighted sum error
    tlog=(1+2/(3000000000000*v))*z+d+(1+1/v)*j+t
    tw=z+d+j+w
    x=tlog/v
    # exp(x)-1 <= x/(1-x) (x>=0, x<1), without cancellation
    tprod=tlog/(1-x)
    res=I(a*L).exp()
    return tprod*res,tlog*res,tw*res

    w=(2*c-1+delta)*(-v/2).exp()+I('2.67')*(-2*v/3).exp()
    t=(2*(1+1/v)*c-1+delta)*(-v/2).exp()+I('2.67')*(1+1/v)*(-2*v/3).exp()

$$

 \mathcal  R(L)&=\mathcal  R(L_N)-T/L_N+E_\theta (L)/L+
                    \int _{L_N}^L E_\theta (v)(1/v+1/v^2)\,dv.
 \end{split}
$$
For $L_N\le  v\le 23.3$, CH2 Lemma 9.2 and the prime-power estimates above imply
$$
 -(1.791001 e^{-v/2}+1.78e^{-2v/3})\le  E_\theta (v)\le -0.19e^{-v/2}.
$$
In anchor.py, for a block ([l,u]) bound the negative endpoint error by the upper negative envelope at $u$ and by the lower negative envelope at $l$, using $1/u,1/l$ in the $\mathcal  R$ bound. For the integral use the interval to $u$ with weight $1/L_N+1/L_N^2$ for the lower side and the interval to $l$ (or zero on the first block) with weight $1/u+1/u^2$ for the upper side. $$

 \qquad |W(L)|\le W_s(L):=\frac{2(3.15\cdot10^{-7})+33(1+2/L)e^{-L/2}}{L}.
$$
The second inequality is (M1) applied to $J_s$; here the floor is integrable against $1/v^2$. The coefficient $33$ pads the explicit CH2 ordinate factor. At $23.3\le L<K$, instead of integrating the looser $\psi$ envelope past $K$, anchor the identities (M1) at $K$. Thus

 |U(L)|&\le J_s(K)+\phi(L)+\phi(K)+\int_L^K\phi,\\
 |W(L)|&\le W_s(K)+\phi(L)/L+\phi(K)/K
                     +(1/L+1/L^2)\int_L^K\phi ,
\end{aligned}
$$

def pure(L,m):
    a,Z,rem=spectralparts(m)
    v=I(L); z=ev(Z,L); d=ev(rem,L); j=im(rem,L)
    w,t=tails(L)
    # L times log error, and weighted sum error
    tlog=(1+2/(3000000000000*v))*z+d+(1+1/v)*j+t
    tw=z+d+j+w
    x=tlog/v

mertens.cpp uses the ordinary Eratosthenes sieve, marking all $p^2,p^2+p,\ldots $ for each unmarked $p\le \sqrt  N$. Every composite has a least prime factor $\le \sqrt  N$, so the unmarked integers (ge2) are exactly primes. All arithmetic for the tests is integer, with scale $F=2^{62}$, unsigned input sizes and signed 128-bit fixed-point intermediates. In the reduced logarithm calculation $1\le  n/d\le 2$, set $z=(n-d)/(n+d)\le 1/3$. Use the lower rounded powers and sum for $2\sum _{j=1,3,dots,41} z^j/j$. The discarded analytic tail is $<1/F$; the rounded $z^2$ has fixed-point error $<5/3$ units, and each rounded odd power error is $<3$ units $one multiplication uses a fac\to r at most (1/9) and the rounding of the fac\to r and \prod uct adds \le ss than (5/3+1)$. Dividing by an odd integer adds at most another unit to the error. Hence the overall lower estimate is within 210 units. Undo powers of two using the same lower bound for $\log  2$; all high logs here use at most 30 shifts, giving total error $\le 6510$ units. For (loglog x) on tested endpoints (xge11), the input error divided by the lower $\log  x>2$, plus the log error with at most four shifts, is below 6511 units. All products fit, including the reduction for (loglog x): when $d=16F$, $n-d<6F$ since $\log  N<22$, and otherwise (dle8F) and $n-d<8F$. Thus $F(n-d)<2^{127}$. Other products (powers, fixed bounds (le F), summands and rational argument numerator at most $1000N$) have smaller widths.

For $\gamma $, use $H_m-\log  m-1/(2m)$ at $m=10^6$ with error $<1/(m-1)^2$ by comparing the integral of $1/t$ to its trapezoidal sums $per unit \int erval error at most (1/(6j^3))$. Fixed-point divisions, summations and rounding pads are explicit in the code. For $M$, add the tail in $[0,1/(2N)]$ of the positive logarithmic prime powers. For $B_3$, the tail of $\sum  \log  p/(p(p-1))$ is in $[.997/N,1.004/N]$: integrate $w(t)=1/(t(t-1))$ against $\theta $, using $|\theta (t)-t|\le 0.0002t$ for $t\ge  N$ from Dusart Thm.4.2 with $k=3,eta_3=.78$. The integral of the main term is $\log (N/(N-1))$ and the error is at most $0.0002(2/(N-1)+\log (N/(N-1)))$. The stated rational bounds hold also at the earlier trial $N=4\cdot 10^8$.

The sieve tests both sides of every relevant prime jump and the terminal endpoint $N$. For product error $\le  q=c/L^3$ it suffices to certify $|Y|\le  q-q^2/2\le \log (1+q)$, since (P,Q) are mutual reciprocals after normalization. All tested bounds are rounded in the adverse direction. Between prime jumps the residual is a constant minus $\log  L$ $\prod ucts and (\mathcal  R)$ or $L$ $(\mathcal  G)$; the absolute value of the slope of its pertinent error budget is smaller than $1/L$ or 1 respectively for (xge11) and these coefficients. Bisection is only a search for a successful tested point, not a proof of optimality. This verifies every real argument after the recorded start and up to $N$. The same finite data give the enclosures at $N$ used in the anchored analytic proof.

def anch(l,u):
    v,w=I(l),I(u)
    negR=(-ev(dn,l)/v-(1/L0+1/L0**2)*im(dn,L0,w)).a
    posR=(-ev(up,u)/w-(1/w+1/w**2)*(im(up,L0,v) if v.a>=L0.b else I(0))).b
    negG=(-ev(dn,l)-im(dn,L0,w)).a
    posG=(-ev(up,u)-(im(up,L0,v) if v.a>=L0.b else I(0))).b
    br=R+I(negR,posR)
    bg=G+I(negG,posG)
    be=I(max(br.b,hi(lambda:br.a.copy_negate()+D('0.00000000025'))))
    return [(be.exp()-1)*w**3,I(max(br.b,br.a.copy_negate()))*w**3,I(max(bg.b,bg.a.copy_negate()))*w**2]
CHSM=[(I('0.000000315'),Q(0),0),(I(33),Q(1,2),0)]
def ws(v):
    t=I(v)
    return (2*CHSM[0][0]+33*(1+2/t)*(-t/2).exp())/t
def after(l,u):
    T=piecewise(l,u)
    if l>=58:return T
    v,w=I(l),I(u)
    tw,tl=tails(l);tl=tl/v
    if l<K:
        t=I(K)
        F=ev(A,l);F0=ev(A,K);J=im(A,l,K)
        U=F+J+F0+ev(CHSM,K)+tw
        W=(F/v)+(1/v+1/v**2)*J+F0/t+ws(K)+tl
    else:
        U=ev(CHSM,l)+tw
        W=ws(l)+tl
    return (mini(T[0],(W.exp()-1)*w**3),
            mini(T[1],W*w**3),mini(T[2],U*w**2))
def chk():
    pi=I('3.14159265358979323846','3.14159265358979323847')
    z=(I(10000000)/(2*pi)).log()
    assert (z*z/(2*pi)-z/(6*pi)).b<33
    assert (pi/9999999).b<D('.000000315')
    assert I(K).exp().a>D('1000000000')

    assert (I(1)-I('166.64')/I(Q(L0.a))**3-I('.791')).a>D('.19')
    l=Q(L0.a);u=Q('23.3')
    beta5=[D(0)]*3
    while l<u:
        r=min(u,l+Q(1,64))
        beta5=[max(x,y.b) for x,y in zip(beta5,anch(l,r))]
        l=r
    print('anchor bridge from x=2e9 through L=23.3',*[f'{x:.9E}' for x in beta5])
    assert all(z<D('.0223') for z in beta5)
    obs=[D(0)]*3
    for l,u in [(Q('23.3'),K),(K,Q(58)),(Q(58),Q(190)),(Q(190),Q(200))]:
        M=[D(0)]*3
        while l<u:
            r=min(u,l+Q(1,64))
            M=[max(v,x.b) for v,x in zip(M,after(l,r))]
            l=r
        print('followup through L=',u,*[f'{x:.9E}' for x in M])
        obs=[max(x,y) for x,y in zip(obs,M)]
    assert all(z<D('.0223') for z in obs)

power=I(Q(int(r),2**100)).a,I(Q(int(s),2**100)).b

# Compute the original gamma enclosure anew, without trusting decimal input.
# Bound log(n) at full interval precision instead of using the old logscaled.
n=10**6
h=sum(F//j for j in range(1,n+1))
g=I(I(Q(h,F)).a,I(Q(h+n,F)).b)-I(n).log()-I(Q(1,2*n))
g+=I(I(Q(-1,(n-1)**2)).a,I(Q(1,(n-1)**2)).b)
print('gamma interval',g)

# Main integral: pointwise finite geometric expansion of 1/(h+u),
# with alternating remainder in the direction of the first omitted term.
v=I(K).log()
def partial(n):
    return sum((-1)**j*factorial(j)/v**(j+1) for j in range(n))/(2*K)
J=I(partial(14).a,partial(15).b)
B=J*I(1,(1+I(Q(2,3*(K-1)))).b)
# g(t) <= (1+2/(3(K-1)))/(2 t^2 log t) on t>=K.
def gt(t):
    return (1+I(Q(2,3*(K-1))))/(2*I(t)**2*I(t).log())
eps=I('.000188')
eps2=I('.001')
assert (I('1.791000147')/I(K)**Q(1,2)+I('1.78')/I(K)**Q(2,3)).b<eps.a
assert (I('20.83')/I(Y).log()**3).b<eps2.a
pad=eps*(2*K*gt(K)+B)+eps2*(Y*gt(Y)+gt(Y)*Y)
T=B+I(pad.b.copy_negate(),pad.b)
M=g-I(*power)-T
print('prime power sum to K',I(*power))
print('main integral',B,'tail correction cap',pad.b)
print('M interval',M)
# Also check the earlier printed values, then find new milligrid starts.
out={}
for r in rows:
    ab=Q(r[3]); a,b,x=int(r[7]),int(r[10]),int(r[-1])
    s,k=counts[a]
    sp=I(I(Q(s,F)).a,I(Q(s+k,F)).b)
    def at(z):
        l=I(Q(z,1000)).log()
        tol=I(ab)/l**3
        return sp-M-l.log(),tol
    def yes(z):
        f,t=at(z)
        return f.b<=t.a and -f.a<=t.a
    assert 1000*a<=x<=1000*b and yes(x)
    l,u=1000*a,x
    while l<u:
        mid=(l+u)//2
        if yes(mid):u=mid
        else:l=mid+1
    assert yes(u)
    out[ab]=u
    print('reciprocal',str(ab),a,b,'old',x,'new',u)

def anch(l,u):
    v,w=I(l),I(u)
    negR=(-ev(dn,l)/v-(1/L0+1/L0**2)*im(dn,L0,w)).a
    posR=(-ev(up,u)/w-(1/w+1/w**2)*(im(up,L0,v) if v.a>=L0.b else I(0))).b
    negG=(-ev(dn,l)-im(dn,L0,w)).a
    posG=(-ev(up,u)-(im(up,L0,v) if v.a>=L0.b else I(0))).b
    br=R+I(negR,posR)
    bg=G+I(negG,posG)
    be=I(max(br.b,hi(lambda:br.a.copy_negate()+D('0.00000000025'))))
    return [(be.exp()-1)*w**3,I(max(br.b,br.a.copy_negate()))*w**3,I(max(bg.b,bg.a.copy_negate()))*w**2]
CHSM=[(I('0.000000315'),Q(0),0),(I(33),Q(1,2),0)]
def ws(v):
    t=I(v)
    return (2*CHSM[0][0]+33*(1+2/t)*(-t/2).exp())/t
def after(l,u):
    T=piecewise(l,u)
    if l>=58:return T
    v,w=I(l),I(u)
    tw,tl=tails(l);tl=tl/v
    if l<K:
        t=I(K)
        F=ev(A,l);F0=ev(A,K);J=im(A,l,K)
        U=F+J+F0+ev(CHSM,K)+tw
        W=(F/v)+(1/v+1/v**2)*J+F0/t+ws(K)+tl
    else:
        U=ev(CHSM,l)+tw
        W=ws(l)+tl
    return (mini(T[0],(W.exp()-1)*w**3),
            mini(T[1],W*w**3),mini(T[2],U*w**2))
def chk():
    pi=I('3.14159265358979323846','3.14159265358979323847')
    z=(I(10000000)/(2*pi)).log()
    assert (z*z/(2*pi)-z/(6*pi)).b<33
    assert (pi/9999999).b<D('.000000315')
    assert I(K).exp().a>D('1000000000')

    assert (I(1)-I('166.64')/I(Q(L0.a))**3-I('.791')).a>D('.19')
    l=Q(L0.a);u=Q('23.3')
    beta5=[D(0)]*3
    while l<u:
        r=min(u,l+Q(1,64))
        beta5=[max(x,y.b) for x,y in zip(beta5,anch(l,r))]
        l=r
    print('anchor bridge from x=2e9 through L=23.3',*[f'{x:.9E}' for x in beta5])
    assert all(z<D('.0223') for z in beta5)
    obs=[D(0)]*3
    for l,u in [(Q('23.3'),K),(K,Q(58)),(Q(58),Q(190)),(Q(190),Q(200))]:
        M=[D(0)]*3
        while l<u:
            r=min(u,l+Q(1,64))
            M=[max(v,x.b) for v,x in zip(M,after(l,r))]
            l=r
        print('followup through L=',u,*[f'{x:.9E}' for x in M])
        obs=[max(x,y) for x,y in zip(obs,M)]
    assert all(z<D('.0223') for z in obs)

def anch(l,u):
    v,w=I(l),I(u)
    negR=(-ev(dn,l)/v-(1/L0+1/L0**2)*im(dn,L0,w)).a
    posR=(-ev(up,u)/w-(1/w+1/w**2)*(im(up,L0,v) if v.a>=L0.b else I(0))).b
    negG=(-ev(dn,l)-im(dn,L0,w)).a
    posG=(-ev(up,u)-(im(up,L0,v) if v.a>=L0.b else I(0))).b
    br=R+I(negR,posR)
    bg=G+I(negG,posG)
    be=I(max(br.b,hi(lambda:br.a.copy_negate()+D('0.00000000025'))))
    return [(be.exp()-1)*w**3,I(max(br.b,br.a.copy_negate()))*w**3,I(max(bg.b,bg.a.copy_negate()))*w**2]
CHSM=[(I('0.000000315'),Q(0),0),(I(33),Q(1,2),0)]
def ws(v):
    t=I(v)
    return (2*CHSM[0][0]+33*(1+2/t)*(-t/2).exp())/t
def after(l,u):
    T=piecewise(l,u)
    if l>=58:return T
    v,w=I(l),I(u)
    tw,tl=tails(l);tl=tl/v
    if l<K:
        t=I(K)
        F=ev(A,l);F0=ev(A,K);J=im(A,l,K)
        U=F+J+F0+ev(CHSM,K)+tw
        W=(F/v)+(1/v+1/v**2)*J+F0/t+ws(K)+tl
    else:
        U=ev(CHSM,l)+tw
        W=ws(l)+tl
    return (mini(T[0],(W.exp()-1)*w**3),
            mini(T[1],W*w**3),mini(T[2],U*w**2))
def chk():
    pi=I('3.14159265358979323846','3.14159265358979323847')
    z=(I(10000000)/(2*pi)).log()
    assert (z*z/(2*pi)-z/(6*pi)).b<33
    assert (pi/9999999).b<D('.000000315')
    assert I(K).exp().a>D('1000000000')

    assert (I(1)-I('166.64')/I(Q(L0.a))**3-I('.791')).a>D('.19')
    l=Q(L0.a);u=Q('23.3')
    beta5=[D(0)]*3
    while l<u:
        r=min(u,l+Q(1,64))
        beta5=[max(x,y.b) for x,y in zip(beta5,anch(l,r))]
        l=r
    print('anchor bridge from x=2e9 through L=23.3',*[f'{x:.9E}' for x in beta5])
    assert all(z<D('.0223') for z in beta5)
    obs=[D(0)]*3
    for l,u in [(Q('23.3'),K),(K,Q(58)),(Q(58),Q(190)),(Q(190),Q(200))]:
        M=[D(0)]*3
        while l<u:
            r=min(u,l+Q(1,64))
            M=[max(v,x.b) for v,x in zip(M,after(l,r))]
            l=r
        print('followup through L=',u,*[f'{x:.9E}' for x in M])
        obs=[max(x,y) for x,y in zip(obs,M)]
    assert all(z<D('.0223') for z in obs)

def anch(l,u):
    v,w=I(l),I(u)
    negR=(-ev(dn,l)/v-(1/L0+1/L0**2)*im(dn,L0,w)).a
    posR=(-ev(up,u)/w-(1/w+1/w**2)*(im(up,L0,v) if v.a>=L0.b else I(0))).b
    negG=(-ev(dn,l)-im(dn,L0,w)).a
    posG=(-ev(up,u)-(im(up,L0,v) if v.a>=L0.b else I(0))).b
    br=R+I(negR,posR)
    bg=G+I(negG,posG)
    be=I(max(br.b,hi(lambda:br.a.copy_negate()+D('0.00000000025'))))
    return [(be.exp()-1)*w**3,I(max(br.b,br.a.copy_negate()))*w**3,I(max(bg.b,bg.a.copy_negate()))*w**2]
CHSM=[(I('0.000000315'),Q(0),0),(I(33),Q(1,2),0)]
def ws(v):
    t=I(v)
    return (2*CHSM[0][0]+33*(1+2/t)*(-t/2).exp())/t
def after(l,u):
    T=piecewise(l,u)
    if l>=58:return T
    v,w=I(l),I(u)
    tw,tl=tails(l);tl=tl/v
    if l<K:
        t=I(K)
        F=ev(A,l);F0=ev(A,K);J=im(A,l,K)
        U=F+J+F0+ev(CHSM,K)+tw
        W=(F/v)+(1/v+1/v**2)*J+F0/t+ws(K)+tl
    else:
        U=ev(CHSM,l)+tw
        W=ws(l)+tl
    return (mini(T[0],(W.exp()-1)*w**3),
            mini(T[1],W*w**3),mini(T[2],U*w**2))
def chk():
    pi=I('3.14159265358979323846','3.14159265358979323847')
    z=(I(10000000)/(2*pi)).log()
    assert (z*z/(2*pi)-z/(6*pi)).b<33
    assert (pi/9999999).b<D('.000000315')
    assert I(K).exp().a>D('1000000000')

    assert (I(1)-I('166.64')/I(Q(L0.a))**3-I('.791')).a>D('.19')
    l=Q(L0.a);u=Q('23.3')
    beta5=[D(0)]*3
    while l<u:
        r=min(u,l+Q(1,64))
        beta5=[max(x,y.b) for x,y in zip(beta5,anch(l,r))]
        l=r
    print('anchor bridge from x=2e9 through L=23.3',*[f'{x:.9E}' for x in beta5])
    assert all(z<D('.0223') for z in beta5)
    obs=[D(0)]*3
    for l,u in [(Q('23.3'),K),(K,Q(58)),(Q(58),Q(190)),(Q(190),Q(200))]:
        M=[D(0)]*3
        while l<u:
            r=min(u,l+Q(1,64))
            M=[max(v,x.b) for v,x in zip(M,after(l,r))]
            l=r
        print('followup through L=',u,*[f'{x:.9E}' for x in M])
        obs=[max(x,y) for x,y in zip(obs,M)]
    assert all(z<D('.0223') for z in obs)

### Entire-domain link

Let $a,b$ be the last uncertified endpoint and its next prime for an old receipt row, and $x_0$ the old sufficient cutoff. The new sieve verifies both primes and *absence* of primes in $(a,b)$, and encloses the sum through $a$. Search inside $[a,x_0]$ for a new certified $y$ at milligrid resolution. Only the **final directed test** at $y$ is used, so search monotonicity at finite precision is not required. On $[a,b)$, the true $\mathcal R$ has derivative $-1/L$ in $L$, so both $\mathcal R-c/L^3$ and $\mathcal R+c/L^3$ strictly decrease because $L^3>3c$. assert (I('20.83')/I(Y).log()**3).b<eps2.a

power=I(Q(int(r),2**100)).a,I(Q(int(s),2**100)).b

# Compute the original gamma enclosure anew, without trusting decimal input.
# Bound log(n) at full interval precision instead of using the old logscaled.
n=10**6
h=sum(F//j for j in range(1,n+1))
g=I(I(Q(h,F)).a,I(Q(h+n,F)).b)-I(n).log()-I(Q(1,2*n))
g+=I(I(Q(-1,(n-1)**2)).a,I(Q(1,(n-1)**2)).b)
print('gamma interval',g)

# Main integral: pointwise finite geometric expansion of 1/(h+u),
# with alternating remainder in the direction of the first omitted term.
v=I(K).log()
def partial(n):
    return sum((-1)**j*factorial(j)/v**(j+1) for j in range(n))/(2*K)
J=I(partial(14).a,partial(15).b)
B=J*I(1,(1+I(Q(2,3*(K-1)))).b)
# g(t) <= (1+2/(3(K-1)))/(2 t^2 log t) on t>=K.
def gt(t):
    return (1+I(Q(2,3*(K-1))))/(2*I(t)**2*I(t).log())
eps=I('.000188')
eps2=I('.001')
assert (I('1.791000147')/I(K)**Q(1,2)+I('1.78')/I(K)**Q(2,3)).b<eps.a
assert (I('20.83')/I(Y).log()**3).b<eps2.a
pad=eps*(2*K*gt(K)+B)+eps2*(Y*gt(Y)+gt(Y)*Y)
T=B+I(pad.b.copy_negate(),pad.b)
M=g-I(*power)-T
print('prime power sum to K',I(*power))
print('main integral',B,'tail correction cap',pad.b)
print('M interval',M)
# Also check the earlier printed values, then find new milligrid starts.
out={}
for r in rows:
    ab=Q(r[3]); a,b,x=int(r[7]),int(r[10]),int(r[-1])
    s,k=counts[a]
    sp=I(I(Q(s,F)).a,I(Q(s+k,F)).b)
    def at(z):
        l=I(Q(z,1000)).log()
        tol=I(ab)/l**3
        return sp-M-l.log(),tol
    def yes(z):
        f,t=at(z)
        return f.b<=t.a and -f.a<=t.a
    assert 1000*a<=x<=1000*b and yes(x)
    l,u=1000*a,x
    while l<u:
        mid=(l+u)//2
        if yes(mid):u=mid
        else:l=mid+1
    assert yes(u)
    out[ab]=u
    print('reciprocal',str(ab),a,b,'old',x,'new',u)
for c,prose in [('0.2',2278382186),('0.15',5001781860),('0.12',8789120961)]:
    assert out[Q(c)]<=prose

def anch(l,u):
    v,w=I(l),I(u)
    negR=(-ev(dn,l)/v-(1/L0+1/L0**2)*im(dn,L0,w)).a
    posR=(-ev(up,u)/w-(1/w+1/w**2)*(im(up,L0,v) if v.a>=L0.b else I(0))).b
    negG=(-ev(dn,l)-im(dn,L0,w)).a
    posG=(-ev(up,u)-(im(up,L0,v) if v.a>=L0.b else I(0))).b
    br=R+I(negR,posR)
    bg=G+I(negG,posG)
    be=I(max(br.b,hi(lambda:br.a.copy_negate()+D('0.00000000025'))))
    return [(be.exp()-1)*w**3,I(max(br.b,br.a.copy_negate()))*w**3,I(max(bg.b,bg.a.copy_negate()))*w**2]
CHSM=[(I('0.000000315'),Q(0),0),(I(33),Q(1,2),0)]
def ws(v):
    t=I(v)
    return (2*CHSM[0][0]+33*(1+2/t)*(-t/2).exp())/t
def after(l,u):
    T=piecewise(l,u)
    if l>=58:return T
    v,w=I(l),I(u)
    tw,tl=tails(l);tl=tl/v
    if l<K:
        t=I(K)
        F=ev(A,l);F0=ev(A,K);J=im(A,l,K)
        U=F+J+F0+ev(CHSM,K)+tw
        W=(F/v)+(1/v+1/v**2)*J+F0/t+ws(K)+tl
    else:
        U=ev(CHSM,l)+tw
        W=ws(l)+tl
    return (mini(T[0],(W.exp()-1)*w**3),
            mini(T[1],W*w**3),mini(T[2],U*w**2))
def chk():
    pi=I('3.14159265358979323846','3.14159265358979323847')
    z=(I(10000000)/(2*pi)).log()
    assert (z*z/(2*pi)-z/(6*pi)).b<33
    assert (pi/9999999).b<D('.000000315')
    assert I(K).exp().a>D('1000000000')

    assert (I(1)-I('166.64')/I(Q(L0.a))**3-I('.791')).a>D('.19')
    l=Q(L0.a);u=Q('23.3')
    beta5=[D(0)]*3
    while l<u:
        r=min(u,l+Q(1,64))
        beta5=[max(x,y.b) for x,y in zip(beta5,anch(l,r))]

        M=[D(0)]*3
        while l<u:
            r=min(u,l+Q(1,64))
            M=[max(v,x.b) for v,x in zip(M,after(l,r))]
            l=r
        print('followup through L=',u,*[f'{x:.9E}' for x in M])
        obs=[max(x,y) for x,y in zip(obs,M)]
    assert all(z<D('.0223') for z in obs)

Put $K=10^8$, $Y=10^{13}$, $f(t)=\sum_{m\ge2}1/(mt^m)$ and $g(t)=f(t)/\log t$ for $t>1$. Determine
$$
 M=\gamma-\sum_{p\le K} f(p)-T,\qquad T=\int_{(K,\infty)}g(t)\,d\theta(t).
$$
For the finite sum, `repair_m.cpp` uses Eratosthenes. At each prime, sum $\lfloor U/(mp^m)\rfloor$ for all $mp^m\le U=2^{100}$. The omitted terms sum to less than $2/U$ per prime since successive summands have ratio less than $1/p\le 1/2$; each retained floor loses less than $1/U$. The printed endpoints pad by the number of retained terms plus twice the prime count. Integer widths suffice: $p\le10^8<2^{27}$ in the power loop, $m\ge2$, so even the subsequent multiplication has $qp\le (U/2)p<2^{126}$; the tested product $qm$ is formed only after passing $q\le U/m$. The total $f$-sum is less than $1$ by $f(t)\le1/(2t(t-1))$ and telescoping over integers. The sieve ceiling is at most $2\cdot10^9$, as are the original 32-bit bounds on loop indices including their last increments. Reciprocal-sum snapshots use one floor at $2^{62}$ per prime and the prime count as padding.

For $\gamma$ use $n=10^6$ and $\gamma=H_n-\log n-1/(2n)+E_n$, where $|E_n|\le(n-1)^{-2}$. Indeed, summing the unit trapezoid differences from $\int dt/t$ from $n$ up gives $E_n$, with each error at most $1/(6k^3)$ on $[k,k+1]$ by integrating the linear interpolation bound with $\sup |(1/t)''|$. Enclose $H_n$ by floors at $2^{62}$ padded by $n/2^{62}$. No external decimal digit of $\gamma$ or $M$ is assumed.

Let $B=\int_K^\infty g(t)dt$, and (J=\int_K^\infty [2t^2\log t]^{-1}dt). Then $J\le B\le(1+2/[3(K-1)]$J) by summing the geometric majorant for $m\ge3$. With $h=\log K$,
$$
 J=\frac{1}{2K}\int_0^\infty\frac{e^{-u}}{h+u}\,du .
$$
The finite geometric identity for $1/(h+u)$ gives inequalities, for every $u\ge0$, between the 14- and 15-term expansions, respectively below and above. Integrating them gives the alternating factorial sums in `repair_m.py`; no use of a convergent infinite factorial expansion is made.

For $K\le t\le Y$, CH2 p.35 Lem.9.2 and Dusart2018 p.13 Cor.4.5 give
$$
 |\theta(t)-t|/t\le 1.791000147/\sqrt t+1.78/t^{2/3}<.000188.
$$
For $t\ge Y$, Dusart p.11 Thm.4.2's global $k=3$ row gives $20.83/\log^3 t<.001$. Let $G(t)=(1+2/[3(K-1)]$/$2t^2\log t$) for $t\ge K$, so $g\le G$. Integration by parts with the right-continuous counting function gives
$$
 |T-B|\le .000188 (2K G(K)+B)+.001\cdot2Y G(Y).
$$
In detail, the boundary at $K$ costs at most $.000188 K g(K)$; the first integral costs at most $.000188\int_K^\infty t(-g'(t))dt=.000188(Kg(K)+B)$. The part with the later error bound costs at most $.001(Yg(Y)+\int_Y^\infty g)$; the last integral is at most $YG(Y)$. The boundary at infinity is zero by these same bounds. This yields
$$
 .26149721284629719<M<.26149721284881525.
$$
The program uses the narrower full directed interval in the receipt. The previously attempted .000181 relative cap at $K$ failed its outward check; .000188 is checked, not assumed.

**Stronger per-observable bridge:** on B0, again with inclusive real endpoints, both product errors are at most \(.02209/L^3\) from \(615614452.413\), the reciprocal error is at most \(.02209/L^3\) from \(615616274.570\), and the weighted error is at most \(.02127/L^2\) from \(1122442236.136\). These and the .02214 rows are separate strength/onset tradeoffs.

The finite sieve changes only the target list as above; `sieve_opt_receipt.txt` gives the endpoints and the unchanged anchor. For the continuation, the same signed argument for `anch` is legal through \(L=24\): \(e^{24}<10^{13}\), the \(.19e^{-v/2}\) signed estimate is verified at \(\log N\) and remains valid by monotonicity of \(d(v)=166.64/v^3\), and the other CH2 and prime-power terms hold on this full interval. The `after` branch is legal already at \(N\) since the \(.791\) seed and the earlier exact-\(K\) transport need only \(10^4\le x\le e^K\). Instead of switching all observables at 23.3, take the **minimum separately** for each observable of the two block bounds on \([\log N,24]\). This yields checked block maxima below .022084, .022084, .021266 in the three normalizations. Through 200 use `after` on the same split domains and the finer \(1/128\) grid; beyond 200 use \(.01880L^2e^{-L/8}<.02127\) and its monotone decrease. No estimated crossing is asserted as a valid switch. Exact executable certificates are `bridge_opt.py` and `sieve_opt.py` and their two receipts.

p=Path(__file__).with_name('mertens.cpp')
s=p.read_text()
i=s.index('   t.push_back({form,223,10000});')
j=s.index('\n }',i)
Path('/work/sieve_opt.cpp').write_text(s[:i]+'   t.push_back({form,form==2?2127:2209,100000});'+s[j:])

def ck():
    assert I(24).exp().b<I(10**13).a
    # Verify the unchanged input-independent domain and sign checks in anchor.chk.
    chk()
    cs=list(map(D,['.02209','.02209','.02127']))
    for i,(l,u) in enumerate([(Q(L0.a),Q(24)),(Q(24),K),(K,Q(58)),(Q(58),Q(190)),(Q(190),Q(200))]):
        M=[D(0)]*3
        while l<u:
            r=min(u,l+Q(1,128))
            v=after(l,r)
            if i==0:
                w=anch(l,r)
                v=[mini(t,z) for t,z in zip(v,w)]
            M=[max(x,y.b) for x,y in zip(M,v)]
            l=r
        assert all(x<c for x,c in zip(M,cs))
        print('opt through',u,*[f'{x:.9E}' for x in M])
    assert (I('.01880')*200**2*(-I(25)).exp()).b<min(cs)

def anch(l,u):
    v,w=I(l),I(u)
    negR=(-ev(dn,l)/v-(1/L0+1/L0**2)*im(dn,L0,w)).a
    posR=(-ev(up,u)/w-(1/w+1/w**2)*(im(up,L0,v) if v.a>=L0.b else I(0))).b
    negG=(-ev(dn,l)-im(dn,L0,w)).a
    posG=(-ev(up,u)-(im(up,L0,v) if v.a>=L0.b else I(0))).b
    br=R+I(negR,posR)
    bg=G+I(negG,posG)
    be=I(max(br.b,hi(lambda:br.a.copy_negate()+D('0.00000000025'))))
    return [(be.exp()-1)*w**3,I(max(br.b,br.a.copy_negate()))*w**3,I(max(bg.b,bg.a.copy_negate()))*w**2]
CHSM=[(I('0.000000315'),Q(0),0),(I(33),Q(1,2),0)]
def ws(v):
    t=I(v)
    return (2*CHSM[0][0]+33*(1+2/t)*(-t/2).exp())/t
def after(l,u):
    T=piecewise(l,u)
    if l>=58:return T
    v,w=I(l),I(u)
    tw,tl=tails(l);tl=tl/v
    if l<K:
        t=I(K)
        F=ev(A,l);F0=ev(A,K);J=im(A,l,K)
        U=F+J+F0+ev(CHSM,K)+tw
        W=(F/v)+(1/v+1/v**2)*J+F0/t+ws(K)+tl
    else:
        U=ev(CHSM,l)+tw
        W=ws(l)+tl
    return (mini(T[0],(W.exp()-1)*w**3),
            mini(T[1],W*w**3),mini(T[2],U*w**2))

all_exact_source_refs.exact_readback: * Real exponent comparisons retain the main M6 curve (from $L\ge62$), all original branches and the exact signed prescription in mertens.md §5. `m_tail_extra_receipt.txt` adds rounded whole-ray M0 coefficients (first three errors (C x^{-a}/L), weighted error (C x^{-a})): B0 $(L_0,C)=(155,.22320),(200,.018791)$; B1 ((155,.51687),(169,.32619),(200,.25973)). At the common onset 200 the ratio $(.25973/.018791)e^{-L/32}$ is already strictly less than 1 and decreases. Moreover $.25973e^{-L/32}<.01$ there, so B1 still beats the established B0 spectral budget floor throughout the common ray. Reusing the M6 ray monotonicity rather than inferring a tail from the grid, fixed error $10^{-14}$ for products and reciprocals is certified from $L=1485/8$ (B0) versus $2667/16$ (B1); weighted $10^{-12}$ from $190$ vs $1357/8$. These are sufficient values, not optimal onsets.

def ck():
    for m in (0,1):
        a,*_=spectralparts(m)
        for L,c in [(155,'.22320' if not m else '.51687'),
                    (169,'.26100' if not m else '.32619'),
                    (200,'.018791' if not m else '.25973')]:
            if m==0 and L==169: continue
            z=pure(Q(L),m)
            assert all(x.b<D(c) for x in z)
            print('clean',m,L,c)
        for kind,limit,lo_,hi_ in [('first','1e-14',150,186 if m==0 else 167),
                                    ('weighted','1e-12',150,190 if m==0 else 170)]:
            def bound(L):
                v=I(L)
                return pure(L,m)[0 if kind=='first' else 2]*(-I(a)*v).exp()/(v if kind=='first' else 1)
            l,r=lo_*16,hi_*16
            assert bound(Q(r,16)).b<D(limit)
            while l<r:
                x=(l+r)//2
                if bound(Q(x,16)).b<D(limit):r=x
                else:l=x+1
            L=Q(l,16)
            H=bound(L)
            assert H.b<D(limit)
            print('fixed',m,kind,limit,L,f'{H.b:.9E}')
    # Matched clean coefficients: strict dominance on overlap L>=200.
    assert (I('.25973')/I('.018791')*(-I(Q(200,32))).exp()).b<1
    assert (I('.25973')*(-I(Q(200,32))).exp()).b<D('.01')

def spectralparts(m):
    a=Q(1,8) if m==0 else Q(5,32)
    S=S0 if m==0 else S1
    Z=S[4:]
    D=S[:4]+[(I(12),a+Q(1,6),4),(I(15),a+Q(1,2),2)]
    return a,Z,D
def pure(L,m):
    a,Z,rem=spectralparts(m)
    v=I(L); z=ev(Z,L); d=ev(rem,L); j=im(rem,L)
    w,t=tails(L)
    # L times log error, and weighted sum error
    tlog=(1+2/(3000000000000*v))*z+d+(1+1/v)*j+t
    tw=z+d+j+w
    x=tlog/v
    # exp(x)-1 <= x/(1-x) (x>=0, x<1), without cancellation
    tprod=tlog/(1-x)
    res=I(a*L).exp()
    return tprod*res,tlog*res,tw*res

def spectralparts(m):

def pure(L,m):
    a,Z,rem=spectralparts(m)
    v=I(L); z=ev(Z,L); d=ev(rem,L); j=im(rem,L)
    w,t=tails(L)
    # L times log error, and weighted sum error
    tlog=(1+2/(3000000000000*v))*z+d+(1+1/v)*j+t
    tw=z+d+j+w
    x=tlog/v
    # exp(x)-1 <= x/(1-x) (x>=0, x<1), without cancellation
    tprod=tlog/(1-x)
    res=I(a*L).exp()
    return tprod*res,tlog*res,tw*res

The antiderivative used for the new initial check is $\log s+\sum_{j\ge1}s^j/(j\,j!)$. On $0<s\le100$, after term 512, subsequent ratios are at most $100/513<1/2$, so the remainder is at most twice the first omitted term. Some earlier starts failed in this implementation; e.g. the initial $P_{28}$ test at 34 and smooth $C$ test at 35 failed. These do not rule out better barriers. $L^4C>H_{70}$ holds for $L\ge95$.

def wide_Finit(L):
    b=I(600).log()
    ps=[p for p in range(2,601) if all(p%d for d in range(2,p) if d*d<=p)]
    c=len(ps)+(600-sum(I(p).log() for p in ps))/b
    def ant(s):
        assert s.a>0 and s.b<=100
        n=512
        z=s.log()
        t=I(1)
        for j in range(1,n+1):
            t=t*s/j
            z+=t/j
        return z+I(0,(2*t*s/((n+1)**2)).b)
    return c+ant(I(L))-ant(b)

H=3000000000000
CZ=(2*I(29).exp()/25+4*I(62).exp()*(ev(CH,58)+ev(powers,58))/58**2)

def setup(m):
    _,Z,D=spectralparts(m)
    return Z,D+powers,CZ+I(62).exp()*ev(Z,T)/(H*62**2)

@lru_cache(maxsize=128)
def osc(l,m):
    Z,D,c=setup(m)
    v=I(l)
    assert l>=62
    return (v**4*ev(Z,l)*(1+(1+2/(v*(Q(3,4)-3/T)))/(H*v))
       + sum(co*v**(4+k)*(-I(a)*v).exp()*(1+1/(v*(1-a-2/T))) for co,a,k in D)
       + c*v**5*(-v).exp())

def osc_loss(l,m):
    x,y=osc(l,m),osc(l-1,m)
    z=I(l)
    return (z/(l-1))**5*y+2*Alim(l)*x+x*x/z**4

def old_loss(l,m):
    return loss(l,l,m,False)

@lru_cache(maxsize=128)
def osc_tail(l,m,K): # controls H_K using first residual from H_70
    j=K-3
    assert l-1>=8*(8+j)

        for m in (0,1):
            start=(8*(8+k-3)+1)*2
            z=find(start,10000,lambda z:osc_tail(Q(z,2),m,k))
            onset.append(Q(z,2))

    for m,c in [(0,100),(1,100),(0,145),(1,145)]:
        j=2 if c<145 else 3
        a=145-c if c<145 else g(7)
        extras=[(j,a)]+[(s-4,g(s)) for s in range(j+5,28)]

            L=Q(z,4)

            L=Q(z,16)

        # Threshold proposals are searched on the mesh; unsuccessful proposals are not claims.

def main_ode(N,L0=34):
    for n in range(4,N+1):assert g(n)>0
    A=lambda L: I(L)*(-I(L)).exp()*Finit(L)
    A0=A(L0)
    P=sum(I(factorial(n))/I(L0)**n for n in range(N+1))
    assert P.b < A0.a and A0.b < Alim(L0).a
    C=I(L0)/(L0-1)*A(L0-1)-A0*A0
    assert (Hmain(L0,N)/I(L0)**4).b < C.a
    # Triangular polynomial source certificate.
    a=[0,0]+[factorial(n)-1 for n in range(2,N)]+[factorial(N)-2]
    d=[sum(a[i]*a[n-i] for i in range(len(a)) if 0<=n-i<len(a)) for n in range(2*N+1)]
    p=[d[j]-(d[j-1] if j else 0) for j in range(len(d))]+[-d[-1]]
    for n in range(4,N+2):
        p[n]-=g(n) if n<=N else 0
        if n>=5:p[n]+=n*g(n-1)
    assert all(v==0 for v in p[:N+1])
    assert p[N+1]+sum(Q(min(c,0),L0**(j-N-1)) for j,c in enumerate(p) if j>N+1)>0

def wide_Finit(L):
    b=I(600).log()
    ps=[p for p in range(2,601) if all(p%d for d in range(2,p) if d*d<=p)]
    c=len(ps)+(600-sum(I(p).log() for p in ps))/b
    def ant(s):
        assert s.a>0 and s.b<=100
        n=512
        z=s.log()
        t=I(1)
        for j in range(1,n+1):
            t=t*s/j
            z+=t/j
        return z+I(0,(2*t*s/((n+1)**2)).b)
    return c+ant(I(L))-ant(b)

H=3000000000000
CZ=(2*I(29).exp()/25+4*I(62).exp()*(ev(CH,58)+ev(powers,58))/58**2)

def setup(m):

@lru_cache(maxsize=128)
def osc(l,m):

    v=I(l)

    x,y=osc(l,m),osc(l-1,m)
    z=I(l)
    return (z/(l-1))**5*y+2*Alim(l)*x+x*x/z**4

def old_loss(l,m):
    return loss(l,l,m,False)

@lru_cache(maxsize=128)
def osc_tail(l,m,K): # controls H_K using first residual from H_70
    j=K-3
    assert l-1>=8*(8+j)
    return (osc_loss(l,m)*I(l)**j).b<I(g(K+1)).a

def find(l,r,test):
    assert test(r)
    while l<r:
        t=(l+r)//2
        if test(t):r=t
        else:l=t+1
    assert test(l)
    return l

    cert.Finit=wide_Finit
    N=70
    main_ode(N,95)
    for k in [26,27,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,69]:
        onset=[]
        for m in (0,1):
            start=(8*(8+k-3)+1)*2
            z=find(start,10000,lambda z:osc_tail(Q(z,2),m,k))
            onset.append(Q(z,2))
        print('profile',k,*onset,flush=True)

    # At four smaller onsets, retain CH and old S bounds in addition to oscillatory.
    # Preselect exploratory positive point values, but certify strips and the analytic tail.
    for m,c in [(0,100),(1,100),(0,145),(1,145)]:
        j=2 if c<145 else 3
        a=145-c if c<145 else g(7)
        extras=[(j,a)]+[(s-4,g(s)) for s in range(j+5,28)]
        def tailpt(z):
            L=Q(z,4)
            return (osc_loss(L,m)*I(L)**j).b<I(a).a
        root=find(4*(8*(8+j)+1),1600,tailpt)
        def pt(z):
            L=Q(z,16)
            return (sum(I(a0)/I(L)**h for h,a0 in extras)-mini(osc_loss(L,m),old_loss(L,m))).a>0
        # Threshold proposals are searched on the mesh; unsuccessful proposals are not claims.
        begin=find(16*(160 if m else 185),4*root,pt)
        ends=Q(root,4)
        L=Q(begin,16)
        buf=Q(1,32)
        while True:
            l=L; good=True
            while l<ends:
                u=min(l+buf,ends)
                val=sum(I(a0)/I(u)**h for h,a0 in extras)
                if val.a<=mini(osc_loss(l,m),loss(l,u,m,False)).b:
                    good=False
                    break
                l=u
            if good:break
            L+=buf
        print('margin',c,'B'+str(m),'onset',L,'tail',ends,flush=True)

def main_ode(N,L0=34):
    for n in range(4,N+1):assert g(n)>0
    A=lambda L: I(L)*(-I(L)).exp()*Finit(L)
    A0=A(L0)

    assert P.b < A0.a and A0.b < Alim(L0).a

A block with insufficient slack is bisected until a directed test passes or the computation rejects at its mesh limit. The $c=7.7$ B0 trial failed a narrow sufficient test on $[484079/2560,968163/5120]$ (near the CH/spectral switch). Neither failure is a counterexample to the true gap.

all_exact_source_refs.exact_readback: * If the resulting $Y$-interval is $[y_-,y_+]$, the two relative errors are bounded respectively by $\max (e^{-y_-}-1,1-e^{-y_+})$, $\max (e^{y_+}-1,1-e^{y_-})$. Take minima separately with Dusart Thm.5.9, the finite certificates and simple whole-ray rows. A direct bound $\delta<1$ on a relative error can also be propagated to the $Y$-interval by taking $[\log(1-\delta),\log(1+\delta)]$ for $Q$ or its negative for $P$, and crossed back to $\mathcal R$ via (M2). Do not use the inverse branch with the same two signed errors without this conversion.

def anch(l,u):
    v,w=I(l),I(u)
    negR=(-ev(dn,l)/v-(1/L0+1/L0**2)*im(dn,L0,w)).a
    posR=(-ev(up,u)/w-(1/w+1/w**2)*(im(up,L0,v) if v.a>=L0.b else I(0))).b
    negG=(-ev(dn,l)-im(dn,L0,w)).a
    posG=(-ev(up,u)-(im(up,L0,v) if v.a>=L0.b else I(0))).b
    br=R+I(negR,posR)
    bg=G+I(negG,posG)
    be=I(max(br.b,hi(lambda:br.a.copy_negate()+D('0.00000000025'))))
    return [(be.exp()-1)*w**3,I(max(br.b,br.a.copy_negate()))*w**3,I(max(bg.b,bg.a.copy_negate()))*w**2]

def pure(L,m):
    a,Z,rem=spectralparts(m)
    v=I(L); z=ev(Z,L); d=ev(rem,L); j=im(rem,L)
    w,t=tails(L)
    # L times log error, and weighted sum error
    tlog=(1+2/(3000000000000*v))*z+d+(1+1/v)*j+t
    tw=z+d+j+w
    x=tlog/v
    # exp(x)-1 <= x/(1-x) (x>=0, x<1), without cancellation
    tprod=tlog/(1-x)
    res=I(a*L).exp()
    return tprod*res,tlog*res,tw*res

def spectralparts(m):
    a=Q(1,8) if m==0 else Q(5,32)
    S=S0 if m==0 else S1
    Z=S[4:]
    D=S[:4]+[(I(12),a+Q(1,6),4),(I(15),a+Q(1,2),2)]
    return a,Z,D
def pure(L,m):
    a,Z,rem=spectralparts(m)
    v=I(L); z=ev(Z,L); d=ev(rem,L); j=im(rem,L)
    w,t=tails(L)
    # L times log error, and weighted sum error
    tlog=(1+2/(3000000000000*v))*z+d+(1+1/v)*j+t
    tw=z+d+j+w
    x=tlog/v
    # exp(x)-1 <= x/(1-x) (x>=0, x<1), without cancellation
    tprod=tlog/(1-x)
    res=I(a*L).exp()
    return tprod*res,tlog*res,tw*res

def ck():
    for m in (0,1):
        a,*_=spectralparts(m)
        for L,c in [(155,'.22320' if not m else '.51687'),
                    (169,'.26100' if not m else '.32619'),
                    (200,'.018791' if not m else '.25973')]:
            if m==0 and L==169: continue
            z=pure(Q(L),m)
            assert all(x.b<D(c) for x in z)
            print('clean',m,L,c)
        for kind,limit,lo_,hi_ in [('first','1e-14',150,186 if m==0 else 167),
                                    ('weighted','1e-12',150,190 if m==0 else 170)]:
            def bound(L):
                v=I(L)
                return pure(L,m)[0 if kind=='first' else 2]*(-I(a)*v).exp()/(v if kind=='first' else 1)
            l,r=lo_*16,hi_*16
            assert bound(Q(r,16)).b<D(limit)
            while l<r:
                x=(l+r)//2
                if bound(Q(x,16)).b<D(limit):r=x
                else:l=x+1
            L=Q(l,16)
            H=bound(L)
            assert H.b<D(limit)
            print('fixed',m,kind,limit,L,f'{H.b:.9E}')
    # Matched clean coefficients: strict dominance on overlap L>=200.
    assert (I('.25973')/I('.018791')*(-I(Q(200,32))).exp()).b<1
    assert (I('.25973')*(-I(Q(200,32))).exp()).b<D('.01')

    cs=list(map(D,['.02209','.02209','.02127']))
    for i,(l,u) in enumerate([(Q(L0.a),Q(24)),(Q(24),K),(K,Q(58)),(Q(58),Q(190)),(Q(190),Q(200))]):
        M=[D(0)]*3
        while l<u:
            r=min(u,l+Q(1,128))
            v=after(l,r)
            if i==0:
                w=anch(l,r)
                v=[mini(t,z) for t,z in zip(v,w)]
            M=[max(x,y.b) for x,y in zip(M,v)]
            l=r

        print('opt through',u,*[f'{x:.9E}' for x in M])

Here $L=\log x$. The normalized Ramanujan margin means $L^6R(x)/x^2$; all quoted margin relations are strict, and the $L$ thresholds are inclusive. The fixed exponent gain is obtained by deducing a zero boundary $27/32$ from the new hypothesis, not by dropping the available $7/8$ QRH theorem or by using the raw direct estimate below its domain. def main():
    cert.Finit=wide_Finit
    N=70
    main_ode(N,95)
    for k in [26,27,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,69]:
        onset=[]
        for m in (0,1):
            start=(8*(8+k-3)+1)*2
            z=find(start,10000,lambda z:osc_tail(Q(z,2),m,k))
            onset.append(Q(z,2))
        print('profile',k,*onset,flush=True)

    # At four smaller onsets, retain CH and old S bounds in addition to oscillatory.
    # Preselect exploratory positive point values, but certify strips and the analytic tail.
    for m,c in [(0,100),(1,100),(0,145),(1,145)]:
        j=2 if c<145 else 3
        a=145-c if c<145 else g(7)
        extras=[(j,a)]+[(s-4,g(s)) for s in range(j+5,28)]
        def tailpt(z):
            L=Q(z,4)
            return (osc_loss(L,m)*I(L)**j).b<I(a).a
        root=find(4*(8*(8+j)+1),1600,tailpt)
        def pt(z):
            L=Q(z,16)
            return (sum(I(a0)/I(L)**h for h,a0 in extras)-mini(osc_loss(L,m),old_loss(L,m))).a>0
        # Threshold proposals are searched on the mesh; unsuccessful proposals are not claims.
        begin=find(16*(160 if m else 185),4*root,pt)
        ends=Q(root,4)
        L=Q(begin,16)
        buf=Q(1,32)
        while True:
            l=L; good=True
            while l<ends:
                u=min(l+buf,ends)
                val=sum(I(a0)/I(u)**h for h,a0 in extras)
                if val.a<=mini(osc_loss(l,m),loss(l,u,m,False)).b:
                    good=False
                    break
                l=u
            if good:break
            L+=buf
        print('margin',c,'B'+str(m),'onset',L,'tail',ends,flush=True)
